hyps.why: Adding a conv on the direct input-to-output path gains most when that path was previously absent.
Edge 0 feeds node 1, which matters more when its outgoing conv edge to the output is strong.
A strong direct conv path already exists, so the extra conv on edge 5 is redundant.
Edge 4 passes node 1's output, which is more useful when node 1 is a conv-processed signal.
Replacing a conv with a skip loses accuracy, unlike replacing none or pooling.
Removing edge 0 cuts off a useful conv path through node 1.
Node 2 carries richer features when edge 1 is a 3x3 conv, so edge 5 can pass them on.
A skip on the direct path already provides a good gradient route, so the gain from a conv on edge 1 is smaller.
Edge 2 only matters when node 1 carries a conv-processed signal.
Replacing a conv with pooling loses accuracy, unlike replacing none.
